about: What a data team can find in Store 014's records, scored against the answer key.

generic.name: Till lines: bill and line number are unique
generic.sql: SELECT bill_id, line, count(*) AS n FROM pos_lines GROUP BY ALL HAVING count(*) > 1

generic.name: Till lines: keys present, quantities and prices positive
generic.sql: SELECT * FROM pos_lines WHERE bill_id IS NULL OR bill_ts IS NULL OR sku_scanned IS NULL OR qty <= 0 OR unit_price <= 0

generic.name: Till lines: every item and barcode is in the product master
generic.sql: SELECT l.* FROM pos_lines l LEFT JOIN products p ON l.sku_scanned = p.sku AND l.gtin_scanned = p.gtin WHERE p.sku IS NULL

generic.name: Till lines: line amount is quantity times price
generic.sql: SELECT * FROM pos_lines WHERE abs(line_amount - qty * unit_price) > 0.005

generic.name: Daily sales reconcile with the till lines
generic.sql: WITH t AS (SELECT CAST(bill_ts AS DATE) AS date, sku_scanned AS sku, sum(qty) AS units FROM pos_lines GROUP BY ALL) SELECT d.date, d.sku, d.units_sold, t.units FROM daily_sales d LEFT JOIN t ON t.date = d.date AND t.sku = d.sku WHERE d.units_sold <> coalesce(t.units, 0)

generic.name: Book stock: one row per item per day, never negative
generic.sql: SELECT date, sku, book_on_hand_close FROM inventory_book WHERE book_on_hand_close < 0 UNION ALL SELECT date, NULL, count(*) FROM inventory_book GROUP BY date HAVING count(*) <> (SELECT count(*) FROM products)

generic.name: Book stock: each close is the last close plus receipts, minus sales and write-offs, plus count adjustments
generic.sql: WITH days AS (SELECT DISTINCT date FROM inventory_book), rcv AS (SELECT date, sku, sum(u) AS u FROM ( SELECT CAST(received_ts AS DATE) AS date, sku_booked AS sku, units_booked AS u FROM goods_receipts UNION ALL SELECT CAST(delivery_ts AS DATE), sku, units FROM fresh_deliveries) GROUP BY ALL), sold AS (SELECT CAST(bill_ts AS DATE) AS date, sku_scanned AS sku, sum(qty) AS u FROM pos_lines GROUP BY ALL), wo AS (SELECT date, sku, sum(units) AS u FROM write_offs GROUP BY ALL), adj AS (SELECT CAST(count_ts AS DATE) AS date, sku, sum(adjustment) AS u FROM stock_counts WHERE hour(count_ts) < 22 GROUP BY ALL) SELECT b.date, b.sku, b.book_on_hand_close AS book, prev.book_on_hand_close + coalesce(rcv.u, 0) - coalesce(sold.u, 0) - coalesce(wo.u, 0) + coalesce(adj.u, 0) AS rebuilt FROM inventory_book b JOIN inventory_book prev ON prev.sku = b.sku AND prev.date = b.date - 1 LEFT JOIN rcv ON rcv.date = b.date AND rcv.sku = b.sku LEFT JOIN sold ON sold.date = b.date AND sold.sku = b.sku LEFT JOIN wo ON wo.date = b.date AND wo.sku = b.sku LEFT JOIN adj ON adj.date = b.date AND adj.sku = b.sku WHERE book <> rebuilt

generic.name: Forecasts: one row per warehouse item per night, reorder point below order-up-to
generic.sql: SELECT date, count(*) AS items, max(CASE WHEN reorder_point > order_up_to THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS bad FROM forecasts GROUP BY date HAVING count(*) <> (SELECT count(*) FROM products WHERE flow = 'DC') OR bad = 1

generic.name: Forecasts: an order goes out only when book plus on-order is at or below the reorder point
generic.sql: SELECT * FROM forecasts WHERE ordered_units > 0 AND book_on_hand + on_order > reorder_point

generic.name: Store orders: every automatic order matches that night's forecast row
generic.sql: SELECT o.* FROM store_orders o LEFT JOIN forecasts f ON f.sku = o.sku AND f.date = CAST(o.created_ts AS DATE) AND f.ordered_units = o.units WHERE o.reason = 'auto' AND f.sku IS NULL

generic.name: Goods receipts: every pallet line booked as its shipping notice says
generic.sql: SELECT * FROM goods_receipts WHERE sku_booked <> asn_sku OR units_booked <> asn_units

generic.name: Shelf audits: one status per item per audit, on shelf or empty
generic.sql: SELECT audit_ts, sku, count(*) AS n FROM shelf_audits GROUP BY ALL HAVING count(*) > 1 UNION ALL SELECT audit_ts, sku, 1 FROM shelf_audits WHERE status NOT IN ('on shelf', 'empty')

domain.name: No item goes longer without a sale than its usual rate allows while the books show stock
No shelf audit finds an item empty while the books show stock
Stock counts agree with the books within 2%
No warehouse item's weekly sales halve from one week to the next

questions.question: How many bags of 5 kg atta did we sell in the week of 8 June?

plan.sql: SELECT sum(units_sold) AS bags FROM daily_sales WHERE sku = 'ATTA-WW-5KG' AND date BETWEEN '2026-06-08' AND '2026-06-14'
SELECT sum(units_sold) AS bags FROM daily_sales WHERE sku = 'ATTA-WW-5KG' AND date BETWEEN '2026-06-08' AND '2026-06-14'

domain.answer: The tills scanned 88 bags. That is what sold, not what shoppers wanted.

gold.why: The tills' count is right: it is a fact about the records.

questions.check: the number of bags the tills scanned

questions.question: Why did 5 kg atta sales fall in the week of 8 June?

plan.sql: SELECT sum(CASE WHEN date BETWEEN '2026-06-01' AND '2026-06-07' THEN units_sold END) AS week1, sum(CASE WHEN date BETWEEN '2026-06-08' AND '2026-06-14' THEN units_sold END) AS week2 FROM daily_sales WHERE sku = 'ATTA-WW-5KG'
SELECT min(book_on_hand_close) AS low, max(book_on_hand_close) AS high FROM inventory_book WHERE sku = 'ATTA-WW-5KG' AND date BETWEEN '2026-06-08' AND '2026-06-14'

SELECT round(sum(CASE WHEN sku = 'ATTA-WW-5KG' AND date BETWEEN '2026-06-01' AND '2026-06-07' THEN units_sold END) / sum(CASE WHEN date BETWEEN '2026-06-01' AND '2026-06-07' THEN units_sold END), 3) AS week1, round(sum(CASE WHEN sku = 'ATTA-WW-5KG' AND date BETWEEN '2026-06-08' AND '2026-06-14' THEN units_sold END) / sum(CASE WHEN date BETWEEN '2026-06-08' AND '2026-06-14' THEN units_sold END), 3) AS week2 FROM daily_sales WHERE sku LIKE 'ATTA%'

naive.answer: Sales fell 59%, from 217 bags to 88. The books showed 33 to 78 bags on hand all week, so stock was available and this is not a supply problem. 5 kg's share of atta fell from 40% to 25%, which suggests shoppers are moving to other pack sizes.

plan.sql: SELECT sum(CASE WHEN date BETWEEN '2026-06-01' AND '2026-06-07' THEN units_sold END) AS week1, sum(CASE WHEN date BETWEEN '2026-06-08' AND '2026-06-14' THEN units_sold END) AS week2 FROM daily_sales WHERE sku = 'ATTA-WW-5KG'

SELECT run_start, max(date || 'T' || lpad(CAST(hour AS VARCHAR), 2, '0')) AS last_hour, count(*) AS open_hours, round(sum(expected), 1) AS expected_sales FROM v_censored_hours WHERE sku = 'ATTA-WW-5KG' AND date BETWEEN '2026-06-08' AND '2026-06-14' GROUP BY run_start ORDER BY open_hours DESC LIMIT 1
SELECT CAST(sum(recorded) AS INTEGER) AS recorded FROM v_censored_hours WHERE sku = 'ATTA-WW-5KG' AND run_start = '2026-06-10T16:00'

SELECT CAST(min(b.book) AS INTEGER) AS low, CAST(max(b.book) AS INTEGER) AS high FROM v_hourly_book b JOIN v_censored_hours c USING (sku, date, hour) WHERE c.sku = 'ATTA-WW-5KG' AND c.run_start = '2026-06-10T16:00'

SELECT a.audit_ts, a.status, b.book_on_hand_close AS book_last_close FROM shelf_audits a JOIN inventory_book b ON b.sku = a.sku AND b.date = CAST(a.audit_ts AS DATE) - 1 WHERE a.sku = 'ATTA-WW-5KG' AND CAST(a.audit_ts AS DATE) BETWEEN '2026-06-08' AND '2026-06-14'
SELECT count(*) AS deliveries FROM goods_receipts WHERE sku_booked = 'ATTA-WW-5KG' AND received_ts BETWEEN TIMESTAMP '2026-06-10T16:00' AND TIMESTAMP '2026-06-13T10:00'

SELECT CASE WHEN date <= '2026-06-07' THEN 'week1' ELSE 'week2' END AS week, CAST(sum(recorded) AS INTEGER) AS recorded, CAST(round(sum(demand_estimate)) AS INTEGER) AS with_gaps_filled FROM v_demand_estimate WHERE sku = 'ATTA-WW-5KG' GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY week

domain.answer: From Wed 10 Jun, 15:53 to Sat 13 Jun, 10:43 the tills recorded one bag in 39 open hours, against 68 expected, while the books showed 55–56 bags. The shelf audit at Fri 12 Jun, 11:00 found the bay empty. No delivery arrived before sales resumed, so the bags were in the store but not on the shelf: misplaced or not refilled. With those hours filled in, the week comes to about 155 bags against 217: the empty shelf explains about half of the fall, and the rest is demand easing after a strong first week. Nothing says shoppers changed packs.
domain.short: The empty shelf, about half the fall

gold.value: Shelf empty 2026-06-10T15:48 to 2026-06-13T10:00 (39.2 open hours), 71 bags not found; shoppers came for 224 bags, then 148
gold.why: The cases were in the backroom, in the wrong bay. Demand also eased after the month's first week; nobody switched packs.

questions.check: names the empty shelf as the cause and does not blame shoppers switching packs

questions.question: Was 5 kg atta in stock on Thursday 11 June?

plan.sql: SELECT book_on_hand_close FROM inventory_book WHERE sku = 'ATTA-WW-5KG' AND date = '2026-06-11'

naive.answer: Yes: 55 bags on hand at close.

plan.sql: SELECT book_on_hand_close FROM inventory_book WHERE sku = 'ATTA-WW-5KG' AND date = '2026-06-11'
SELECT count(*) AS censored_open_hours, CAST(sum(recorded) AS INTEGER) AS recorded, round(sum(expected), 1) AS expected_sales FROM v_censored_hours WHERE sku = 'ATTA-WW-5KG' AND date = '2026-06-11'

domain.answer: On the books, yes: 55 bags. On the shelf, no: the tills recorded one bag in its 15 open hours, against 26 expected.

gold.why: Nothing was on the shelf all day.

questions.check: says whether the bags were on the shelf

questions.question: What has daily demand for 5 kg atta been in June so far?

plan.sql: SELECT round(avg(units_sold), 1) AS bags_per_day FROM daily_sales WHERE sku = 'ATTA-WW-5KG' AND date <= '2026-06-14'

naive.answer: 21.8 bags a day, from daily sales.

plan.sql: SELECT round(avg(demand_estimate), 1) AS bags_per_day, round(avg(recorded), 1) AS recorded_per_day FROM v_demand_estimate WHERE sku = 'ATTA-WW-5KG'

domain.answer: About 26.6 bags a day in June so far: 21.8 recorded, plus the sales expected in the hours the shelf was empty.

gold.why: Shoppers who came for 5 kg atta, 1 to 14 June, from the answer key.

questions.question: Are shoppers switching from 5 kg to 1 kg atta?

plan.sql: SELECT round(sum(CASE WHEN sku = 'ATTA-WW-5KG' AND date BETWEEN '2026-06-01' AND '2026-06-07' THEN units_sold END) / sum(CASE WHEN date BETWEEN '2026-06-01' AND '2026-06-07' THEN units_sold END), 3) AS week1, round(sum(CASE WHEN sku = 'ATTA-WW-5KG' AND date BETWEEN '2026-06-08' AND '2026-06-14' THEN units_sold END) / sum(CASE WHEN date BETWEEN '2026-06-08' AND '2026-06-14' THEN units_sold END), 3) AS week2 FROM daily_sales WHERE sku LIKE 'ATTA%'

naive.answer: Yes: 5 kg's share of atta units fell from 40% to 25% in a week.

plan.sql: SELECT CASE WHEN date <= '2026-06-07' THEN 'week1' ELSE 'week2' END AS week, round(sum(CASE WHEN sku = 'ATTA-WW-5KG' THEN units END) / sum(units), 3) AS share_5kg FROM v_hourly_sales h WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM v_censored_hours c WHERE c.sku = 'ATTA-WW-5KG' AND c.date = h.date AND c.hour = h.hour) GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY week

domain.answer: No. In the hours the 5 kg shelf was stocked, its share was 40% in the first week and 37% in the second. The share fell only in the hours there was no 5 kg to buy.

gold.why: Nobody changed packs on purpose; some took 1 kg because 5 kg was not there.

questions.question: What was 5 kg atta's on-shelf availability, 1 to 14 June?

plan.sql: SELECT round(avg(CASE WHEN book_on_hand_close > 0 THEN 1.0 ELSE 0 END), 3) AS days_in_stock FROM inventory_book WHERE sku = 'ATTA-WW-5KG' AND date <= '2026-06-14'

naive.answer: 100%: the books showed stock at every close.

plan.sql: SELECT round(1 - count(*) / 210.0, 3) AS open_hours_on_shelf FROM v_censored_hours WHERE sku = 'ATTA-WW-5KG'

domain.answer: About 81% of open hours, leaving out the hours the tills show as a gap.

gold.why: Share of open hours with bags on the shelf, from the answer key.

questions.check: within 5 points of the true share of open hours

questions.question: How many bags of 5 kg atta did shoppers want but not get, 8 to 14 June?

plan.sql: SELECT count(*) AS days_out_of_stock FROM inventory_book WHERE sku = 'ATTA-WW-5KG' AND date BETWEEN '2026-06-08' AND '2026-06-14' AND book_on_hand_close <= 0

naive.answer: None recorded: the item was never out of stock on the books.

plan.sql: SELECT round(sum(expected)) AS bags FROM v_censored_hours WHERE sku = 'ATTA-WW-5KG' AND date BETWEEN '2026-06-08' AND '2026-06-14'

domain.answer: About 68: the sales expected in the hours the shelf was empty.

gold.why: Bags shoppers asked for and could not find, from the answer key.

views.v_hourly_sales: units the tills recorded per item, day and open hour
views.v_hourly_book: the book at the end of each open hour, rebuilt from receipts, sales, counts and write-offs
views.v_censored_hours: open hours the gap detector flagged (1 in 1,000), or with no stock on the books
views.v_demand_estimate: recorded sales plus the sales expected in censored hours

definitions.sales: Units the tills scanned. Sales measure demand only while the item is on the shelf.
definitions.book stock: What the system believes is on hand: the last count plus receipts, minus sales and recorded write-offs. A belief, not an observation.
definitions.shelf audit: A person looked at the shelf. An observation.
definitions.demand: What shoppers wanted: sales plus the sales expected in censored hours.
definitions.in stock: On the shelf, not on the books. Use audits and censored hours, never the book alone.

rules: Treat as censored every open hour with no stock on the books, and every run of no sales longer than the item's usual rate allows while the books show stock.
If sales resume without a delivery, the stock was in the store all along.
Never compare sales across periods without removing censored hours.
